newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Former S.Korean spy chief held in graft scandal.
newsitem.headline: Former S.Korean spy chief held in graft scandal.

text.p: A former top intelligence official close to President Kim Young-sam's disgraced son was arrested on Monday, live television pictures showed.

Kim Ki-sup was shown being hustled into a car outside prosecution offices in Seoul for a trip to prison. He will be charged with taking a 150 million won ($168,000) bribe to help a businessman obtain a lucrative cable television licence.
Television reports said he was on his way to the Seoul Detention House to join the president's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, who was arrested on Saturday.
Kim Ki-sup, looking grim-faced, posed briefly for photographers before getting into the black car. He has denied taking bribes.

State prosecutors allege he took the money from a former executive of Daeho Construction Co in return for help winning a cable television licence. The president's son was also charged with receiving kickbacks from the businessman, Lee Sung-ho.

Kim Ki-sup was a manager at a luxury Seoul hotel before becoming deputy director of the Agency for National Security Planning after President Kim took power. He had been a loyal supporter of Kim Young-sam.
